Consult Summary:
- Reproductive-age woman with several days of worsening lower abdominal pain and light vaginal bleeding; differential includes ovarian cyst rupture, pregnancy-related etiologies (possible early intrauterine pregnancy or ectopic), and pelvic inflammatory disease; plan includes prompt abdominal examination and pregnancy testing with further imaging/treatment as indicated.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Severe lower abdominal pain, ongoing for a few days; pain described as constant and increasing in intensity, about 8/10.
- Location/character: Lower abdomen, midline, below the umbilicus.
- Associated symptoms: Light pink vaginal bleeding/discharge; nausea with occasional vomiting; constipation last week (recent bowel movements mostly normal this week); no fever.
- Menstrual/Contraception: Last menstrual period approximately 2–3 weeks ago; regular but variable bleeding on implant contraception (Implanon) for about 1 year; periods described as sometimes irregular but present; last intercourse about 4 days ago; last pregnancy test about a month ago; no pregnancies to date.
- Pregnancy considerations: Pregnancy test today recommended; patient has an implant; pregnancy status remains a consideration given vaginal bleeding and abdominal pain.
- Sexual activity/Contraception: Sexually active; on Implanon; no other contraception mentioned.
- Medical history: Amoxicillin allergy.
- Social history: Occupation – school teacher; lives with husband and his family; has traveled abroad more than a year ago; current smoking/drinking not clearly documented.
- Review of systems: No dyspnea, chest pain, or urinary symptoms reported; no weight loss; able to continue daily activities though pain is uncomfortable.
- Prior imaging/labs: One prior pregnancy test about a month ago; no current imaging results available.

Past Medical History:
- Allergies: Amoxicillin.
- Medical conditions: None reported besides allergy.
- Surgeries: None reported.
- Pregnancies: None reported.

Medications:
- Implanon (contraceptive implant) in place for about 1 year; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- No other medications documented.
- Allergies: Amoxicillin.

Social History:
- Occupation: Teacher.
- Living situation: Lives with husband and husband’s family.
- Travel: Has traveled abroad in the past; no recent travel reported.
- Substance use: Smoking and alcohol use not clearly documented.
- Reproductive history: Currently on contraception (implant); sexually active; no pregnancies to date.

Family History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Exam findings: Not recorded.
- Note: A face-to-face abdominal examination is planned; no bedside exam data available from this transcript.

Investigations:
- Pregnancy testing: Recommended today; patient to perform pregnancy test now; results not available in this encounter.
- Imaging: Abdominal/pelvic ultrasound not yet performed; planned if indicated after clinical exam.
- Other labs: Not documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Overall Impression:
  - Working impression: Acute lower abdominal/pelvic pain in a reproductive-age woman with light vaginal bleeding, on Implanon; etiologies to consider include ovarian cyst rupture/corpus luteum cyst, pregnancy-related processes (ectopic or threatened/early intrauterine pregnancy), and pelvic inflammatory disease. Ongoing symptoms warrant physical examination and pregnancy testing to guide imaging and management.
- DDx Integration (brief):
  - Ovarian cyst rupture / corpus luteum cyst:
    - Supporting: lower midline abdominal pain, constant and worsening; light vaginal bleeding.
    - Opposing: no imaging yet to confirm; pain location not clearly unilateral.
  - Pregnancy-related (ectopic or threatened abortion/early intrauterine pregnancy):
    - Supporting: vaginal bleeding with lower abdominal pain in a reproductive-age patient; recent menses and implant history; pregnancy test today recommended.
    - Opposing: implant reduces likelihood of pregnancy but does not eliminate risk; no current pregnancy test result yet.
  - Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID):
    - Supporting: lower abdominal pain with vaginal discharge/bleeding in a sexually active young woman.
    - Opposing: no fever or cervical motion/tubal tenderness documented; limited data on discharge/confirmatory signs.
  - Implant-related irregular bleeding:
    - Supporting: on Implanon with irregular bleeding patterns.
    - Opposing: pain is prominent and persistent beyond typical implant-related symptoms.
- Issue 1: Acute lower abdominal pain with midline location and light bleeding
  - Assessment: Differential includes ovarian cyst pathology or early pregnancy-related processes; symptoms warrant evaluation.
  - Plan:
    - Obtain a formal abdominal/pelvic examination in clinic.
    - Perform pregnancy test today; if positive or concern for ectopic, escalate urgently.
    - Arrange pelvic ultrasound as indicated after exam to evaluate ovarian/uterine structures and possible free fluid.
    - Provide supportive care for pain as appropriate; monitor for worsening symptoms.
    - If pain worsens or she cannot keep fluids down, she should seek urgent care.
- Issue 2: Pregnancy-related etiology (including ectopic or threatened abortion)
  - Assessment: Pregnancy status remains in differential until test results are available.
  - Plan:
    - Complete pregnancy testing today (urine/serum as available).
    - If positive: follow obstetric/gynecologic protocol appropriate for location of pregnancy (emergency assessment if ectopic suspected; ultrasound to confirm intrauterine vs extrauterine pregnancy).
    - If negative: continue evaluation for non-pregnancy etiologies (ovarian/pelvic pathology, PID) with imaging as indicated.
- Issue 3: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) considerations
  - Assessment: Possible given vaginal discharge/bleeding and pelvic pain; not enough data to confirm.
  - Plan:
    - If exam or imaging suggests PID, initiate guidelines-based management (antibiotics, partner notification as indicated) per local protocols.
    - Consider STI screening and testing as indicated; discuss risks and counseling.
- General plan:
  - Schedule in-person abdominal/pelvic examination at a clinic.
  - Complete pregnancy testing today; results will guide next steps.
  - If symptoms escalate, return or seek urgent care promptly.
  - Reassess with imaging (pelvic ultrasound) and clinical correlation after exam and test results.
  - Provide patient education on warning signs requiring immediate care (heavy bleeding, severe pain, fever, vomiting with inability to keep fluids down).

Document Quality:
- Missing but clinically expected elements for a consult: Vital signs and explicit physical exam findings are not recorded; no imaging results available yet.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None detected; transcript-guided plan is aligned with broad DDx considerations.
- Transcript quality: Conversation captured essential symptom details, but exam findings and vitals are not documented; clear plan to obtain exam and tests.
